name: Cornishware
summary: White earthenware kitchen ware with four blue hand-banded stripes. It started as a set of storage jars and grew to jugs, mugs and egg cups, in a pattern that a lathe repeats by hand.

philosophy.core_thesis: A kitchen set looks right when every piece carries the same four blue stripes on white, so the shelf reads as one plain family.
design_principles: Make every piece in white earthenware with a wall 3 to 5 mm thick and a plain, round shape.
Band the piece on a banding wheel with four blue stripes: two thick and two thin.
Use one blue, a deep cobalt, in the stripes, and keep the rest white.
Mark the side of a canister with its name in black lettering.
Put a plain lid with a knob on each jar; make the size steps 1, 2 and 3.
Glaze the piece in a clear, bright, white-looking glaze and fire it at about 1060 °C.
Add a pale blue or a cream in later pieces only after 1960.
anti_patterns: A bare ground with no stripe
A gold rim on the lip

form.shape: Storage jars and canisters in graduated sizes, jugs, mugs, bowls, egg cups, rolling pins and teapots.
form.profile: A straight or barrel-shaped wall; a jug has a rounded belly and a short neck; a lid is a flat disc with a knob.
form.foot_and_rim: A flat, glazed foot; a plain, rounded rim; a flat lid that sits in a ledge.
form.proportion: A canister stands 9 to 20 cm high; wall 3 to 5 mm; the stripes are 4 to 15 mm wide.
rules: Put four stripes on every piece, in the same order and widths.
Letter the contents on the front in black capitals.
Keep the forms plain and round.

bodies.rule: Use a white earthenware that takes a bright clear glaze. The body must stay white so that the blue stripes stand out.

methods: slip casting for jugs and teapots
hand banding on a banding wheel
forming.joins: Cast handles are fettled and fixed with slip; lids are cast in a plaster mould to fit the ledge.
forming.details: The stripes are slightly uneven where the hand runs the brush; the lettering is in black stamp type.

glaze.pattern: Four horizontal blue stripes in groups of two thick and two thin, with the name of the contents in black capitals on the front of a canister.
glaze.gloss: A bright gloss of about 80 to 95 GU.
glaze.wear: The blue stripes sit under the glaze and stay clear; the glaze crazes in a fine net on old pieces.

palette.strategy: Blue on white only, with black lettering as the one other colour.

firing.kiln: A gas or coal-fired tunnel kiln; biscuit firing, banding and a clear glaze firing.
processes: banding the stripes by hand on the wheel
firing.scale: A factory of several hundred workers; the range reached more than 30 shapes and sold in the millions.
firing.signs: Four blue stripes that vary a little from piece to piece, and black lettering on the front.

pieces.form: Canister with four blue stripes and the word SUGAR in black
Milk jug with four blue stripes and a strap handle
Mixing bowl with four stripes outside and a white inside
Butter dish with a flat lid and a printed mark

positive: 1920s English blue and white striped kitchenware
black capital lettering on a canister
still-life museum photograph, soft north light

canonical_works.work: Storage jar set in four sizes
Kitchen scale with a blue-banded bowl

emotion.target_response: A neat, cheerful order: the viewer sees four blue stripes and thinks of a tidy shelf in a cottage or a seaside kitchen.

use_cases: a museum label on blue-banded earthenware
a canister or jug brief with a strict four-stripe pattern
avoid_when: the brief needs hand-trailed or sponge decoration
the brief needs an oven dish

modifiers.how: Use fawn, brown and ochre bands on a cream body and add a mocha tree.
Change to a white glass-ceramic body and a printed blue floral decal.
